name: default
decision_reason: baseline

name: use_rrt_connect=true
hypothesis: A_straight 0% because unidirectional RRT* can't thread the ~110m side-corridor detour within the 3s timeout (z-sampling clamped to [-6,0] forbids over-wall route; goal_sample_rate is a dead knob, _smart_sample hardcodes 0.2). Bidirectional RRT-Connect's greedy connect marches through the wide corridor reliably -> converts 15000 in failure penalties into real profile energies.
decision_reason: score 15000->3191.2, min_success 0.0->1.0 (all 3 scenarios 100%)

name: smoother: proxy-guided local search (remove/move/chamfer/split)
hypothesis: A_straight wastes ~930J/run because sharp corners (e.g. 98.6deg overshoot corner at x=74.7) cap entire adjacent long legs at v_turn=sqrt(3*min(L1,L2)/theta). Metric rewards few corners with long balanced legs, NOT fine arcs (chords shrink min(L) -> slower). Proxy-guided moves (vertex remove/relocate, coarse chamfer, collinear split to isolate slow zones) with e/m(v)~150/v-1.6 fit should recover most of it.

name: smoother v3: +split-bend compound move, relocation reach 16m + diagonals
hypothesis: A residual ~480J sits in the 2 topologically unavoidable corners (~70-82deg final corner caps ~58m at ~7m/s). Single moves can't split a sharp corner into two gentle long-legged ones (collinear split alone shrinks minL -> proxy worse -> rejected = local minimum); compound insert+perpendicular-bend in one candidate escapes it.

name: smoother v4: +double-bend move (replace sharp corner with two spread vertices)
hypothesis: Remaining sharp corridor corners (~70deg, vcap~7) need two-gentle-corner geometry; single insertions reach it only via multi-move sequences the greedy proxy rejects midway; a one-candidate double-bend (remove P, insert Q1,Q2 outward) reaches it directly.
decision_reason: score 2540.4->2537.8 (-0.1%, A only 1055->1053; B/C unchanged) — smoother lever saturating, next try planner-side

name: step_size=3.0
hypothesis: Smoother saturated; residual is raw-skeleton quality. Longer greedy RRT-Connect strides (3.0m vs 1.5m) give straighter skeletons and better topology in the ~8-10m corridors -> lower post-smoothing energy at same success.

name: step_size=4.5
hypothesis: step_size ladder continues: 3.0 gained 8.2%, corridors ~8-10m still admit 4.5m strides -> straighter skeletons.
decision_reason: score 2328.9->2294.8 (-1.5%); A 1030->1009J, B 650->637J, C ~flat — diminishing returns

name: step_size=6.0
hypothesis: If skeleton straightness still binds, 6.0m strides gain a bit more; if the corner-geometry floor dominates, this rung flatlines.
decision_reason: score 2347.5 > best 2294.8 (A 1025, B 664, C 659 — all slightly worse; ladder peaked at 4.5, big strides overshoot in corridors)

name: smoother v5: 3D climb/descent proxy + over-wall macro-route probe (REJECTED)
hypothesis: Frozen BEMT makes descent nearly free (desc@12=1.6 J/m vs level 8.2, climb 15.1) -> over-wall climb-cruise-descend template (true 582J idealized) should beat the 93m lateral detour (1205J); inject templates + climb-aware proxy.
decision_reason: score 2327.9 > best 2294.8. Probe never fired: symmetric f2<=0.8 templates descend INTO Row4's back face (descent must start after x~64, f2~0.92) -> all collision-rejected; meanwhile descent-credit proxy encouraged z-wiggles in local moves, A 1009->1043. Idea stays alive: feasible steep-descent over-wall estimates ~840J vs 1009. Next: f2 grid {0.85,0.9,0.95}, conservative descent credit (K_DN=1.0, floor 15W), limit z-relocation steps.

name: smoother v6: late-descent templates + conservative descent credit (REJECTED)
hypothesis: v5's probe failed on template feasibility (descent through Row4); f2 in {0.8..0.95} + K_DN=1.0/floor15 + capped z-steps should let the over-wall route fire.
decision_reason: score 2328.6 > best 2294.8; probe STILL never fired — raw 4-pt template proxy is dominated by the steep-descent corner capping the whole ~59m cruise (phantom-cap), while the incumbent path is compared post-polish. Probe must polish templates BEFORE comparing (and collision-check before the proxy gate). A's +34J regression = proxy-shape side effect on local moves.

name: smoother v7: polish-before-compare over-wall probe (3D ranker) [episode boundary: lit search distilled into KNOWLEDGE]
hypothesis: Over-wall (~840J true) loses to lateral (1009J) only in raw-template proxy form (steep-descent corner phantom-caps the cruise leg); collision-check first, polish feasible templates with the unchanged v4 sweeps, compare via climb-aware 3D ranker -> probe fires where it truly wins.
decision_reason: score 2294.8->2084.0 (-9.2%); A 1009->798.6J (-21%, over-wall route adopted), B/C identical to v4 (probe correctly selective)

name: smoother v8: 3D-aware re-polish after level polish (NO-OP)
hypothesis: A's over-wall path wastes ~150J on a level-proxy-shaped hump (z=-15.2 vs needed -11.5, climb ~18.6 J/vertical-m); re-polishing the adopted route with the 3D proxy should lower it.
decision_reason: byte-identical to v7 (score equal, not lower). 3D re-polish accepts zero moves: hump removal needs coordinated multi-vertex lowering (single-vertex z-move creates an apex corner, correctly rejected). Next: polish adopted templates with 3D proxy FROM THE START (level pass is what builds the hump), or add a plateau-lowering compound move.

name: smoother v9: 3D-proxy polish from raw template (REJECTED)
hypothesis: The -15.2m hump exists because the first polish pass is climb-blind; polishing the raw template directly under the 3D proxy keeps cruise near -11.5 -> A ~700J.
decision_reason: score 2191.8 > best 2084.0; A 798.6->906.3. CONFIRMED PATTERN: pessimistic level proxy beats accurate 3D proxy for local moves even on climb paths (overestimated mid-speed costs push high-vcap corner geometry the true evaluator rewards more than hump removal). Hump needs a dedicated coordinated-lowering move (3D-accepted) ON TOP of level-proxy polish.

name: smoother v10: coordinated hump-lowering pass (NO-OP)
hypothesis: A's hump wastes ~3.4m climb (~60-90J); coordinated run-lowering (3D-accepted, after level polish) removes it where single-vertex moves hit the apex-corner ridge.
decision_reason: byte-identical again — every lowering rejected by the 3D proxy itself: the hump BUYS the 26.4m climb leg its uncapped v* (lowering sharpens the apex corner, caps it at ~14 m/s, costing more than the climb saving). A~799J is near the family floor; hump was a correct trade-off, not waste.

name: step_size=5.0 [episode 2 boundary: racing-line lit + corner-conservation law distilled]
hypothesis: With v7's probe decoupling A from skeleton quality, B/C dominate step_size sensitivity; their optimum may sit between the tested 4.5 and 6.0 rungs.
decision_reason: score 2142.3 > best 2084.0; A identical (probe-dominated ✓), B 637->661, C 648->683. step_size ladder fully resolved: 4.5 is a sharp optimum (3.0 < 4.5 > 5.0 > 6.0).

name: smoother v11: finer probe grid (zc down to -11.2, 5x4 f-grid, top-3 polish)
hypothesis: A's template starts from a coarse grid; finer/lower zc seeds the polish in a slightly better basin (~10-30J).
decision_reason: score 2084.0->2082.0 (-0.1%); A 798.6->796.6J. Floor confirmed — grid refinement yields only ~2J.

name: max_iterations=10000 (knob resolution probe)
hypothesis: RRT-Connect converges far below 5000 iters under the 3s timeout with fixed seeds -> deterministic no-op; confirming closes the last open Layer-1 parameter.
decision_reason: byte-identical (score equal). ALL Layer-1 params now resolved: step_size=4.5 optimal, use_rrt_connect essential, max_iterations dead, goal_sample_rate dead (hardcoded 0.2), search_radius/weight_* dead in Connect branch.

name: smoother v12: extended f-grid edges f1=0.05, f2=0.97 (NO-OP)
hypothesis: The f-grid may clip the basin edge; gentler-climb/later-descent seeds could give the polish a better start.
decision_reason: byte-identical — winning template is interior to the existing grid. Floor 2082.0 confirmed from all directions.

hypothesis: Greedy farthest-first shortcut fixes corners at visibility-jump artifacts; a corner-cap-aware DP over raw polyline vertices finds better min(L)/theta skeletons for B/C; 3D-rank adoption gate protects A.
